title: Kill switch
subtitle: Emergency stop for every AI agent on this server, or for one agent. Stopping takes one click; starting again needs the approval of two different user accounts and a review afterwards.

banner.estateBody: Agents cannot act until two user accounts approve starting again: sessions end, and tool calls, MCP, schedules, voice, model calls, deployments and event delivery are refused.
banner.agentBody: The stopped agents cannot act: their tool calls, MCP calls and other actions are refused.
banner.none: Nothing is stopped. Sessions and agents run normally.

engage.title: Emergency stop
engage.caption: Stops all agents, or one agent: running sessions end, and tool calls, MCP, schedules and workflows, voice, model calls, deployments and event delivery are refused. Pending approval requests for these actions are canceled. Stopping needs no approval; starting again does. The console, the audit trail and sign-in keep working.
engage.agentRefHint: Agent UUID or external reference. An unknown ref still engages — the stop then matches on that exact string.
engage.reasonHint: Required: say why. The review of this stop and later audits read it.
engage.confirmBodyEstate: Every agent stops at once: running sessions end, their actions are refused, and pending approval requests for those actions are canceled. To start again, two different user accounts must approve, and the stop must be reviewed afterwards. There is no emergency way around this.
engage.confirmBodyEstateNoRestart: Every agent stops at once: running sessions end, their actions are refused, and pending approval requests for those actions are canceled. There is no emergency way around this.
engage.confirmBodyAgent: This agent stops at once: its actions are refused and its pending approval requests are canceled. To start it again, two different user accounts must approve, and the stop must be reviewed afterwards.
engage.doneBody: Stop {{id}} is active. Re-enabling requires dual-control.
engage.alreadyStopped: An active stop for this scope already exists
engage.restartNeedsAdmins: Starting again needs two other admin accounts to approve it and one of them to review it afterwards.

stops.title: Stops
stops.caption: Each stop: who started it, when, what it covers, why, and how it was ended and reviewed. Every action checks these stops before it runs.
stops.label: Kill-switch stops
stops.aalHint: Recorded assurance level of the engaging session (forensics; engage itself is never gated on AAL).
stops.revokedHint: Pending approval requests canceled by this stop.
stops.emptyHint: When the kill switch is engaged — by an operator or a guardian rule — the stop appears here.
stops.truncatedHint: There are more stops than shown. This page selects the first 1000 by id — not by when the stop was engaged — so a recent freeze can be missing, and search and sorting apply only to what is loaded. A stop not shown here does not demonstrate that its scope is no longer frozen: the list carries both active and reenabled rows.

reenable.title: Re-enable this stop
reenable.body: Starting again is never one person's decision: two different user accounts must approve, and no one can approve their own request. {{stepUp}} There is no emergency way around it, because staying stopped is the safe state. The engine checks that the accounts are different; it cannot check that two different people use them.

stepUp.none: The extra check for administrative actions is off on this server, so each approver approves with their usual sign-in.
stepUp.totp: Each approver must have signed in with an authenticator code or with single sign-on that used MFA, or confirm with a passkey, unless an approval rule lowers this action's risk level; the two-account rule holds even then.
stepUp.passkey: Each approver must confirm with a passkey (AAL3), unless an approval rule lowers this action's risk level; the two-account rule holds even then.
stepUp.unknown: Each approver must pass this server's extra check for administrative actions, unless an approval rule lowers this action's risk level; the two-account rule holds even then.

reenable.reasonHint: Optional — carried on the dual-control request for the approvers.
reenable.existingApproval: A dual-control approval ({{id}}) is already open for this stop. Checking reports its progress and completes the re-enable once both accounts approved.
reenable.pendingBody: Two distinct user accounts must approve this request in the approvals queue. Check again to complete the re-enable once they have decided.
reenable.reviewDue: Agents run again. The review of this stop is now due.

review.title: Post-review this incident
review.body: The forced post-review closes the incident loop and unblocks the next re-enable of this scope. Separation of duties: whoever engaged, requested or executed the re-enable cannot review it.
review.noteHint: Mandatory — what happened, was the stop justified, what changed.

evidence.doneBody: Tamper-evident incident pack {{file}} — timeline, dual-control proof, findings and rollback plan.
evidence.truncated: Evidence pack downloaded — but it is BOUNDED
evidence.truncatedBody: {{file}} is saved, and the engine capped its timeline or findings. It is not the whole incident: read the truncation flags at the head of the file before drawing conclusions from it.

guardian.title: Guardian rules
guardian.caption: Automatic responses to security findings. A rule matches findings by kind and minimum severity and runs one response, at once or after one person approves it. A rule never reacts to the kill switch's own findings, so one stop cannot set off another.
guardian.name: Rule
guardian.label: Guardian rules
guardian.emptyHint: Author a rule to contain high-risk findings automatically or behind one human approval.

delete.title: Delete guardian rule {{name}}?
delete.description: Pending approval-mode containments of this rule will be CANCELLED. The executed action trail is preserved as evidence. Recreating a rule with the same name will not inherit dedup suppression.

create.title: New guardian rule
create.body: Authoring auto-containment is enforcement-posture authoring — audited. Only an enabled rule ever acts, and containment executions are idempotent.
create.name: Name
create.kindsHint: Comma-separated finding kinds to match; empty matches any kind. The guardian's own 'killswitch_*' / 'guardian_*' findings are always excluded.
create.minSeverityHint: Findings below this severity never match (default high).
create.agentTierHint: Narrows the rule to agents at this tier. Leave it as any and the rule applies to every tier.
create.actionHint: The single containment the rule fires.
create.modeHint: Auto acts immediately and notifies; approval queues the containment behind one human decision.

trail.title: Recent guardian actions
trail.caption: What each rule did — or queued — per matched finding.
trail.label: Guardian actions
trail.emptyHint: When an enabled rule matches a finding, its containment lands here.

guardian.truncated: Loaded the first {{n}} rules by id
guardian.truncatedHint: There are more guardian rules than shown; this page selects the first 1000 by id. A rule not shown here does not demonstrate that it is disarmed — the list carries both enabled and disabled rules.
guardian.trailTruncated: Loaded the first {{n}} actions by id
guardian.trailTruncatedHint: There are more contained actions than shown; this page selects the first 1000 by id, not by `executed_at` — an action created pending can execute much later. A record not shown here does not demonstrate that it does not exist: it may be pending, executed, rejected, expired or failed.
